basis: algebra: |B| S - (|B+| - |B-|) |B| V_hat = 2 |B+||B-| (Vbar+ - Vbar-) for S the sum of c_obs, divided by 2 |B| V_hat; exact rational residual 0 on all 171 units of the five retained IBM runs (the replica mean and every replica of the ibm_fez kernel map, the ibm_fez and ibm_marrakesh coset maps and the ibm_fez and ibm_kingston parallel coset runs) and on 192 wide placements, double-precision residual at most 7.1e-15 and 4.4e-16; the unit tests check a grid of class sizes and the loader against the group summarize; the domain excludes undecided bins (the four-term blocks read levels) and requires |V_hat| above the code guard of 1e-9
falsifier: a residual above 1e-12 on a contrast vector with every bin decided and |V_hat| above 1e-9; none on the retained runs

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston
claim: A coset block whose XOR pairs are all aligned (N_b = 4 on 8 bins, B- empty) reads N_hat = 4 whatever the device did, for any contrast vector with |V_hat| above 1e-9, and a block with B+ empty reads -|B-|/2; every other block reads a function of the data, so N_b below 4 (0, 1, 2 or 3) marks the blocks that carry hardware information
basis: with B- empty V_hat = Vbar+ = S/|B+| and N_hat = |B+|/2 (A5-228); 52 forced units over the ibm_fez and ibm_marrakesh coset maps and the ibm_fez and ibm_kingston parallel coset runs (11 to 17 replicas each) read 4 with largest departure 0.0 over every replica, replica visibility 0.54 to 0.94, no replica under the guard, and the stored readout-corrected value equals 4 on 40 of 40 blocks; the self-test replaces the arm laws of an N_b = 4 block by seven fixed count edits and requires 4 to 1e-12, while the same edits move an N_b = 0 block by at least 0.05; N_b = 1 and 3 occur in 384 blocks each of the 3,720 default-tiling blocks of the 930 two-term operands (the nullity counts equal census.json), so the informative set is N_b below 4 and not {0, 2}
falsifier: a block with B- empty and |V_hat| above 1e-9 whose N_hat differs from |B+|/2

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston
claim: The nullity-8 and nullity-12 N_hat readings of the coset-block runs (ibm_fez coset map 8.05, 12.02, 12.14 for e1 + e10, e1 + e18, e1 + e24) carry most of their integer by algebra: two of four blocks (e1 + e10, e1 + e24) or three of four (e1 + e18, e17 - e2) are forced to 4, and the measurement is the sign map (all 32 signs on every operand) with the informative blocks
basis: ibm_fez coset map replica-mean blocks: e1 + e18 0.0151, 4, 4, 4 (12.0151); e1 + e24 2.080, 4, 2.057, 4 (12.137); e1 + e10 0.020, 4, 0.030, 4 (8.050); e1 + e26 2.064, 0.058, 2.052, 0.058 (4.233); all four coset runs give the same pattern and the whole deviation from the nullity lies in the informative blocks (0.004 to 0.039 on the VB operands e1 + e18 and e17 - e2); the 32-bin estimator on the same contrasts reads 12.23 to 12.38 on the nullity-12 operands (Vbar+ above Vbar- by 0.055 to 0.088), 0.09 to 0.37 above the block sum; half the sum of the signs equals the nullity on every operand of the four runs

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez full kernel map
claim: The ibm_fez full-map N_hat is bin-independent: the class means Vbar+ and Vbar- of the per-output contrasts agree, so N_hat returns the nullity whatever the visibility of the circuit
basis: replica mean of c(y) over 5 replicas: Vbar+ exceeds Vbar- on 7 of 8 circuits (null operand 0.3754 against 0.3150, e1 + e26 0.1221 against 0.0466, e2 + e27 0.1899 against 0.1340, e1 + e18 0.1430 against 0.1131, e1 + e24 0.1410 against 0.1198); the per-replica class gap (4 degrees of freedom, two-sided p, Bonferroni over 8 circuits) is significant on e2 + e27 alone (t 8.27, p 0.0093 corrected) and not on e1 + e26 (t 4.28, p 0.013 uncorrected, 0.10 corrected), the null operand (2.11) or the others, so the refutation of a bin-independent contraction rests on e2 + e27 and the 7 of 8 sign of the gaps; by the identity of A5-228 the replica-mean N_hat reads 1.40, 10.04, 6.48, 9.17, 12.75, 12.54 for nullity 0, 4, 4, 8, 12, 12 (bias +1.40, +6.04, +2.48, +1.17, +0.75, +0.54), where averaging the per-replica N_hat gives 1.54, 34.09, 8.25, 7.30, 12.65, 8.37; A5-180 keeps its sign-network claim and its intervals, which include the ideal values; the stated premise (hypothesis-level in the code) is falsified, and the conditional statement of the code stays exact
falsifier: an ibm_fez full-map run whose class gaps lie within the 2.776 critical value (4 degrees of freedom) of zero on every operand

claim: The aligned-pair profile of the default coset tiling separates the nullity-12 orbits V and VB of two-term operands, so the ibm_fez block readings [2.08, 4, 2.06, 4] of e1 + e24 and [0.02, 4, 4, 4] of e1 + e18 discriminate the orbits
basis: census of the 252 two-term operands of nullity 12 (hardware_orbits.classify): the sorted profile (0, 4, 4, 4) holds 12 operands, all VB; (2, 2, 4, 4) holds V 24, VB 108, V^a- 6, V^a+ 6; (3, 3, 3, 3) holds V 32, VB 48, V^a- 8, V^a+ 8; the profile depends on the 3-dimensional subspace (e1 + e18 reads [0,4,4,4], [2,2,4,4], [3,3,3,3] under (19,1,2), (19,2,4), (19,4,8)); the profiles do separate the two measured operands, ideal [2,4,2,4] against [0,4,4,4], measured on four coset runs with block differences 2.054 to 2.069 and -1.938 to -1.964 at 65.6 to 136.9 standard errors, where the second block compares a measured block with a forced value; a reading [0,4,4,4] under the default tiling excludes V among two-term operands of nullity 12, and a reading [2,4,2,4] does not identify V
falsifier: an operand of orbit V with sorted profile (0, 4, 4, 4) under its default tiling, or a tiling-independent profile statistic that separates the orbits

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston

claim: The fiber ring k[y]/K2 of W8 is a tensor product of two algebras on 12 fiber generators each (the twist J(z) + J(z') of A5-223 lifts from the base ideal to the fiber ring)
basis: Macaulay's bound: h_1 = 24 gives 12 generators per half, and h_2 = 156 (A5-139) leaves 144 degree-2 products across the halves, so the degree-2 values of the halves sum to 12; the maximum of h_3 over the splits is 167 (the extreme split 12 + 0: Macaulay bound 23 for the half with h_2 = 12, plus 144), against the measured lower bound h_3 >= 551 at N = 9 (the W8 degree-3 row of the findings note, 551 <= h_3 <= 600); the doubled base ideal of A5-223 does not lift to the fiber ring
falsifier: a measured h_3 of W8 at or below 167, or a proof that k[y]/K2 of W8 splits with a different generator count

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston
claim: The N_b = 2 and N_b = 3 coset-block bias follows a local output-bit channel at a flip rate near 0.021 per bit: the block contractions fall with Hamming weight and multiply, and the rate fitted on the four coset runs predicts the wide runs' ratio of N_b = 3 to N_b = 2 bias (1.10 predicted, 1.32 +- 0.25 measured, against 0.58 for a constant class gap per visibility)

falsifier: a new N_b = 3 to N_b = 2 bias ratio below 0.8 on placements whose null controls pass, or a per-bit channel fit that a readout-plus-final-layer error model of the same qubits cannot reach

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston

fibers: A_5 two-term operands, ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh and ibm_kingston
claim: All-aligned coset blocks carry a bin-dependent contraction that no tensor-product readout channel produces, hidden from N_hat by the forced law: 15 of 52 forced blocks reject flatness at p < 0.05 on three of four runs, a count whose family-level significance is not yet calibrated against the dependence among blocks
basis: Hotelling T^2 on the 7 within-replica deviation coordinates (flatness_hotelling_p) is a valid test per block: p < 0.05 on 15 of 52 forced blocks (2.6 expected if independent), p < 0.001 on 1; the binomial tail 2.3e-8 and the per-run Fisher combinations 1e-6, 2e-6 (ibm_fez), 0.0018 (ibm_marrakesh), 0.26 (ibm_kingston) treat the blocks as independent, while blocks of one run share replicas, calibration and compiled circuits, so they describe the count and do not calibrate a family p-value; bin spread 0.007 to 0.011 (about a quarter of the N_b = 2 class gap); the earlier chi-square tails (19 of 52 at p < 0.001) ignored the finite replica count and the residual covariance
falsifier: a run-level permutation or replica-block bootstrap null that keeps the covariance among blocks of one run and gives a family p at or above 0.05 on ibm_fez, or a rerun whose forced blocks read flat within replica noise on the same placements

basis: pooled raw against pooled corrected: 34.08 -> 31.79 (e1 + e26), 8.25 -> 8.00 (e2 + e27), 10.41 -> 11.14 (twin); paired lambda_16 - lambda_0 over five replicas (result_spectral.json minus_zero, minus_zero_t) -0.155, -0.118, -0.066 (t -3.8, -5.4, -2.1) at nullity 4 and +0.103, +0.081, +0.059 (t 2.9, 1.5, 4.7) at nullity 12; the dominant-power alternative fails on the cocycle-free control e1 + e18; reading formed after the data; hypothesis: the orientation qubit decays at an operand-dependent rate set by the compiled SELECT

claim: F(I) is Cohen-Macaulay for X+ -> N+ and X- -> N-
